subject: Governing law & preservation language — Silverline MSA redlines
thread_summary: External legal/procurement sent MSA redlines with governing law = Delaware; Redwood proposes split approach (NY law, arbitration for monetary claims, court access for injunctive relief). Internal legal provided proposed draft text; external asked for an exec one-pager and DocuSign next steps.

Maria — thanks for sending and for the quick turnaround.

High-level: Redwood wants to avoid being litigated in jurisdictions that materially increase discovery and service risk for our hosted and VPC customers. Our preference historically has been New York law for commercially negotiated MSAs; we also use streamlined arbitration language for money claims. That said, we recognize the commercial need for a narrow injunctive relief carveout for IP and data preservation.

Proposed path:
- We can offer New York as the governing law (commercially neutral for both parties).
- Keep arbitration for monetary claims, but allow either party to seek provisional injunctive relief in New York courts to preserve IP/data while the arbitration proceeds.
- Add explicit service-of-process and escalation contacts to the order form to avoid surprise jurisdictional notices.

Looping in David and Laura to draft the exact language — David, can you propose redline text that mirrors our standard arbitration + injunctive-relief carveout? Laura, heads-up in case this needs an exec uplift if Silverline pushes for Delaware instead.

If Silverline is insistent on Delaware, please let us know what commercial levers (e.g., limited venue for injunctions only, or a narrow consent-to-service clause) would help bridge it.

Best,
Ava Chen
Head of Partnerships (Sales)
Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com

Ava / Maria — attaching a short draft (Redwood_GovLaw_Proposal.docx) with language we typically use. Key points in the draft:

1) Governing law: New York law, without regard to conflict-of-law rules.
2) Dispute resolution: binding arbitration (JAMS) for monetary claims under Section 14(a).
3) Injunctive relief carveout: either party may seek provisional injunctive or other equitable relief in the state or federal courts located in New York County, NY, limited to preservation of intellectual property or emergency data preservation; such proceedings shall not be considered a waiver of the obligation to arbitrate remaining claims.
4) Service clause: an order-form annex that designates in-state counsel and a process agent for Silverline for jurisdictional convenience.

I kept the injunctive relief carveout narrowly tailored to IP/data and added a mutual-statement that the parties will use reasonable efforts to coordinate any emergency relief with the arbitrator to avoid duplicative proceedings.

If Silverline prefers Delaware for governing law, an alternative is: keep NY courts for emergency injunctive relief but have Delaware law govern (we can offer that as a fallback). That tends to be acceptable in a small number of deals.

Please let me know if you want me to convert the draft into a redline against Silverline_MSA_Redline_v3.pdf; I can produce a tracked redline and a one-page summary for procurement.

David Kim
